extracted.intended_audience: national football associations, confederations, match organisers, team administrators, and match officials
extracted.subtask_description: Official regulations governing organisation, match operations, discipline, stadium and media requirements for the FIFA World Cup preliminary competition (team entry, player lists, matchday procedures, infrastructure, media and commercial rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary suspensions for cautions and red cards
rubrics_metrics.description: If a player receives two cautions in two different matches, he will be automatically suspended from his team’s subsequent match. If a player is sent off as a result of a direct or an indirect red card, he will be automatically suspended from his team’s subsequent match. In addition, further sanctions may be imposed in the case of a direct red card.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic single-match suspensions apply for two separate cautions or any red card; direct red cards may trigger additional sanctions beyond the automatic suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry-over of suspensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any suspension that cannot be served during this competition will be carried over to the representative team’s next official match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unserved suspensions are applied to the team's next official match outside the competition if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIFA ownership of commercial rights
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA is the original owner of all rights emanating from the final competition and from the preliminary competition as a collective whole, as well as from any other related events coming under its jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights include financial, audiovisual/radio recording, reproduction/broadcasting, multimedia, marketing/promotional, incorporeal (emblems), and copyright-related rights, without restrictions as to content, time, place and law, subject to provisions in specific regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Media and Marketing Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA has issued Media and Marketing Regulations for the Preliminary Competition and shall issue regulations for the Final Competition. All FIFA members must comply with these Media and Marketing Regulations and ensure their members, officials, players, delegates and affiliates also comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations must follow detailed Media and Marketing Regulations when exploiting rights or implementing media/marketing activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for confederation implementation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to FIFA’s approval, confederations are authorised to issue implementation rules and operational guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confederation-level rules must be consistent with FIFA approval and overarching regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry form submission and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Associations shall complete and submit the official FIFA entry form for the preliminary competition via a dedicated extranet online registration in accordance with the deadline stipulated in the relevant FIFA circular. Only entry forms duly registered by the deadline are valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission is online via FIFA extranet; late or unregistered entry forms will not be considered unless FIFA decides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional list of prospective players (contents and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each association shall provide FIFA with a provisional list of prospective players no later than 30 days before its first qualifying match, showing each player’s last name, first name(s), current club, date of birth and passport number, and the head coach’s last name, first name(s), date of birth and nationality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is not binding; further players may be added up to the day before a qualifying match. The list should be as extensive and realistic as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid proof of player identity and nationality
rubrics_metrics.description: The only document considered valid proof of a player’s identity and nationality is a permanent international passport that explicitly, and in Latin characters, states the player’s first name(s), surname(s), and full date of birth. Identity cards or other local documents are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participating associations must present each player’s valid permanent international passport to the FIFA Match Commissioner the day before the match; a player without a valid passport is not entitled to play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start list size and goalkeeper requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The start list must contain a minimum of 14 and a maximum of 23 players, one of which must be a goalkeeper. The 11 first-named players must start the match; the remaining players are substitutes. (Original text set start list at 23 players: 11 starters and 12 substitutes; replacement text allows 14–23 players and at least one goalkeeper up to three.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fewer than 14 players are available, FIFA may consider exceptions on a case-by-case basis. The number 1 shirt is reserved for one goalkeeper. Guidance reflects both original 23-player model and amended 14–23 flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Player shirt numbers and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Players shall wear numbers corresponding with the start list (numbers 1–23 only). All goalkeepers and the captain must be identified as such. Each player shall wear a number between 1 and 23 on the front and back of his shirt and on his shorts; number colour must contrast clearly with the shirt/shorts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers must be legible for stadium spectators and television viewers. It is not compulsory for the player's name to appear on the shirt during the preliminary competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of start list to referee and copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Both teams must return their start list to the referee at least 85 minutes before kick-off and provide the referee with two copies. The opposing team can request one of these copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start list must be completed and signed by the team administrator prior to return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-kickoff replacement of named starters
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of the first 11 players named on the start list are unable to start, they may be replaced by any of the available substitutes; the replaced players may no longer take part in the match and the quota of substitutes is reduced accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After start lists are returned and signed but before kickoff, replacements are permitted; the original text limited in-match substitutions to three, replacement text allows up to five substitutions during the match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of bench quota for unavailable substitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: If any substitutes named on the start list are unable to be fielded on the bench, they may not be replaced on the bench by an additional player, reducing the quota of substitutes accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the match the number of permitted substitutions applies (originally three, with replacement text permitting up to five).

rubrics_metrics.name: Removed players may remain on bench and doping control eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Although no longer eligible to play as a substitute, any injured or ill player who was removed from the start list may be seated on the substitutes’ bench and would then also be eligible for doping control selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removed players are excluded from play but remain subject to anti-doping procedures if present on the bench.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional substitute for extra time
rubrics_metrics.description: One additional substitute may be used when a match goes into extra time (regardless of whether the team has already used the permitted quota of substitutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allowance applies even if the ordinary substitution quota was already exhausted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitutes' bench composition and required officials
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than 23 people (11 officials and 12 substitutes) shall be allowed to sit on the substitutes’ bench. The names of these officials must be indicated on the 'Officials on the Substitutes’ Bench' form to be provided to the FIFA Match Commissioner. A suspended player or official will not be allowed to sit on the substitutes’ bench.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement text requires the bench list to include, at minimum, the head coach, medical doctor and team administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of electronic/communication devices in technical area
rubrics_metrics.description: Small, hand-held electronic or communication devices are permitted in the technical area if used for coaching/tactical purposes or for player welfare, in accordance with the Laws of the Game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Devices must be used only for permitted purposes and comply with Laws of the Game and competition instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority over competition format and draw
rubrics_metrics.description: The FIFA Organising Committee, based on confederation needs and proposals, decides on the format of play, match calendar and group formation for the preliminary competition; any seeding per confederation is based on the FIFA/Coca-Cola World Ranking and the Committee's decisions are final and not subject to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary draw details will be communicated by FIFA and confederations; committee discretion is broad and final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted competition formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Matches may be played in one of three formats: (a) groups home-and-away with three points for a win (league); (b) one home and one away match per team (knockout); (c) by exception and with FIFA Organising Committee permission, a tournament in one country or on neutral territory. Playoffs may be played as one single match by exception with permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a tournament match is abandoned due to insufficient players, the tournament should proceed when possible and FIFA will decide. Changes of format after competition start need Organising Committee approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home match venue country restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: When played in format (a) or (b), home matches may not be played in another country without the express permission of the FIFA Organising Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations must seek prior approval to designate another country as home venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: League format ranking and tie-breakers (primary criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: In league format the ranking in each group is determined by: (a) greatest number of points obtained in all group matches; (b) goal difference in all group matches; (c) greatest number of goals scored in all group matches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary ranking uses total points, then goal difference, then goals scored across all group matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: League format ranking and tie-breakers (head-to-head and further criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more teams are equal on the above, rankings are determined by: (d) greatest number of points obtained in group matches between teams concerned; (e) goal difference from matches between teams concerned; (f) greater number of goals scored in matches between teams concerned; (g) away goals count double between teams concerned (if tie only between two teams); (h) fair play points system with deductions for yellow/red cards; (i) drawing of lots by the FIFA Organising Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fair play deductions: first yellow = -1; second yellow/indirect red = -3 (text shows both '-3' and an apparent typo '-4' — official fair play table to be consulted); direct red = -5; yellow + direct red = [value blank in chunk]. Final resort is drawing of lots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tournament group tie-breakers
rubrics_metrics.description: If a tournament is played in one country/neutral territory and two or more teams are equal after group stage according to criteria 6a–6f, the final rankings will be determined by fair play points (6h) and drawing of lots (6i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie-breakers follow the league criteria then fair play and lots where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification of best runners-up
rubrics_metrics.description: If best second- or third-placed teams qualify for the next stage or final competition, the criteria to decide such teams shall depend on the competition format and require approval of FIFA following confederation proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details vary with format; confederations must propose criteria and obtain FIFA approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined continental qualification paths require FIFA approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed competition format includes a combined qualification path via another continental competition (e.g., completion of last segment or continental playoffs played as single matches), prior approval by FIFA is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any cross-competition qualification arrangements need FIFA sign-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knockout format aggregate and away-goals rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In knockout format both teams play home and away; the team scoring most goals over two games qualifies. If equal, away goals count double. If still equal, extra time of two 15-minute periods is played at the end of the second leg; extra time is part of the second-leg match. If no goals in extra time, kicks from the penalty mark decide the winner according to Laws of the Game. If both teams score same number of goals in extra time, the visiting team is declared the winner on the basis of away goals counting double.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Away-goals rule applies both after regular time and in extra time; extra time and penalties follow Laws of the Game procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-match playoff extra time and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: In playoff matches played as a single match, if level at the end of normal time extra time of two 15-minute periods is played, with a five-minute interval at the end of normal time but not between extra-time periods. Players remain on the pitch between full-time and extra time and between extra-time periods. If still level after extra time, kicks from the penalty mark determine the winner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard extra-time and penalty procedures apply; logistical details (intervals, players remaining on pitch) are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match dates scheduling and dispute resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Match dates are set by the associations concerned and/or the confederation in compliance with the international match calendar and subject to approval by the FIFA Organising Committee. The FIFA general secretariat shall be informed per deadlines. If associations cannot agree on dates the Organising Committee shall decide. Committee ensures simultaneous matches when required for sporting reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations must follow calendar windows and consult FIFA where disputes or special scheduling needs arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue selection, inspection and notification timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Venues are set by the host association and/or confederation and matches may only be played in stadiums inspected and approved by the confederation. Opponents and the FIFA general secretariat shall be notified at least three months before the match. The venue should be no further than 150 km from nearest international airport (max 2-hour drive) and airport should handle charter flights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement text modifies notification to at least eight weeks before the match; if associations cannot agree, the Organising Committee decides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue accommodation and IMP amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The venue must have sufficient high-standard hotels to accommodate the home team, the visiting team and the FIFA delegation. The venue must be able to accommodate amendments needed to implement IMP (International Match Protocol) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host must ensure hotel capacity and logistical capability to meet IMP and FIFA delegation needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kick-off time notification and change approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Host association must inform opponents and FIFA of the kick-off time at least 60 days before the match. If host requests a change, written approval of visiting team must be obtained at least 30 days before. After that deadline only FIFA may approve a late change based on well-founded and documented reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict timelines govern kick-off changes to allow visiting teams and stakeholders to plan travel/operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team arrival and travel itinerary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Associations must arrange their teams to arrive at the venue no later than the evening before the match. FIFA and host association shall be informed of visiting association travel itinerary at least one week in advance. Visiting association must arrange visas if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notification facilitates accreditation, security and logistical arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: COVID-19 testing provisions and IMP compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating member associations must ensure provisions for COVID-19 testing are in place per IMP requirements, considering travel arrangements and laboratory capacity to deliver required results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host and visiting associations must coordinate testing protocols in accordance with IMP and local directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visiting team training session day-before
rubrics_metrics.description: On the day before the match and weather permitting, the visiting team is entitled to one 60-minute training session on the pitch where the match will take place. The time and duration shall be mutually agreed and confirmed in writing by the host association. If the FIFA Match Commissioner cancels due to severe weather, visiting team may inspect the pitch wearing training shoes. If both teams wish to train at the same time, visiting team has priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training arrangements should be confirmed in advance; cancellations due to weather are handled by Match Commissioner with inspection alternatives provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host obligation to notify and bear costs if pitch unfit not notified
rubrics_metrics.description: If the host association considers the pitch unfit, they shall immediately inform FIFA, confederation, visiting association and match officials before departure. If the host fails to inform and the pitch is unfit, the host shall be obliged to pay all expenses incurred for travel, board and lodging of the parties involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely communication mitigates costs and travel disruption; failure to inform can trigger financial liability for host.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee authority on pitch condition
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is doubt regarding pitch condition after the visiting association has already left, the referee shall decide whether the pitch is playable. If declared unplayable, the procedure in the regulations (art. 5 par. 7) is followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referee's safety and playability call is final in-match-related pitch concerns, following specified procedures for postponement or abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Floodlighting and emergency power requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Matches played at night may only be played in stadiums where floodlighting meets minimum FIFA lighting requirements: whole pitch evenly lit, recommended level of at least 1,200 lux. An emergency power generator must guarantee at least two-thirds of that intensity in case of power failure. FIFA may grant exceptions in specific circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host must ensure certified lighting and emergency power; exceptions are discretionary and rare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match promotion and branding
rubrics_metrics.description: All matches in the preliminary competition shall be identified, promoted and advertised as qualifying matches in accordance with the relevant FIFA Media and Marketing Regulations and branding guidelines for the preliminary competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts must apply FIFA branding and promotion rules for consistency across competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stadium technical standards and contingency equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Stadiums and facilities must fulfil requirements in 'Football Stadiums: Technical Recommendations and Requirements' and comply with safety and security standards and other FIFA regulations. Fields of play, accessory equipment and facilities must be in optimum condition and comply with the Laws of the Game. Each stadium shall have spare goals, nets and corner flags in close proximity and an emergency generator fully operational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts must ensure field, equipment and contingency capacity to meet FIFA technical publications and match needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic stadium safety checks and certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Periodic safety checks shall be carried out on selected stadiums. If requested, associations shall provide FIFA and the confederation with a copy of the relevant safety certificate, not more than one year old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement text adds that host association shall put in place comprehensive COVID-19 preventative measures per IMP and additional safety checks for spectators, players and officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stadium inspection for new or refurbished venues
rubrics_metrics.description: Only stadiums inspected and approved by the relevant confederation may be selected; if a stadium no longer complies with FIFA standards, FIFA may reject selection. Brand-new or refurbished stadiums must be inspected prior to use and final inspection applications filed with confederation as stipulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection timing and filing requirements follow confederation rules to ensure compliance before hosting matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: All-seater stadium rule and spectator admission conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general rule matches may only be played in all-seater stadiums. If only stadiums with seating and standing areas are available the standing space shall remain vacant and FIFA Stadium Safety and Security Regulations apply to spectator areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement text qualifies spectator admission as subject to government directives: if spectators are allowed then matches must be in all-seater stadiums, standing spaces vacated, and FIFA safety regulations applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal-line technology consent and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: If host has certified goal-line technology and wishes to use it, both teams must sign FIFA’s consent form. Process: host sends consent form to visiting team; installation must be certified (valid on day of match); completed form submitted to FIFA for information; process completed at least seven days before the match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent and certification steps are mandatory and time-bound to ensure technology validity and team agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retractable roof decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: If a stadium has a retractable roof, the FIFA Match Commissioner, in consultation with the referee and team officials, shall decide before the match whether the roof shall be open or closed; decision is announced at match coordination meeting and may be modified prior to kick-off if weather changes. If match starts with roof closed it remains closed; if it starts open and weather deteriorates roof may be closed and remain closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions balance playing conditions and safety, with Match Commissioner and referee holding authority during match coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted pitch surfaces and quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Matches may be played on natural or artificial surfaces or hybrid systems. Artificial surfaces must meet FIFA Quality Programme for Football Turf or International Match Standard unless dispensation is given. If artificial surface used, visiting team is entitled to two practice sessions before the match if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surface certification required; dispensation is exceptional and visiting teams are given practice opportunities on artificial turf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warm-up area allocation and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each stadium shall have sufficient space for warm-ups, ideally behind the goals. Maximum of six players may warm up at same time with max two officials; only goalkeeper may warm up with a ball. If insufficient space, both teams warm up in designated area beside substitutes’ bench of team B behind assistant referee no.1 with max three players and one official per team and without any balls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement text specifies designated warm-up areas may be allocated behind each team’s substitutes’ bench with max three players and one official per team without any balls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match clocks, added time and half-time interval
rubrics_metrics.description: Clocks showing time played may run during the match but shall be stopped at the end of normal playing time in each half (after 45 and 90 minutes) and after 15 minutes of each extra-time half. Half-time interval shall be 15 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible stadium clocks must reflect referee-determined stoppage indications and be stopped at official period ends as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee indication of added time
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the two periods of normal playing time the referee shall indicate to the fourth official, either orally or by gesturing, the number of minutes decided to allow for time lost; this also applies to extra-time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referee communicates added time to fourth official for display and match control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of substitution panels and display boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels or electronic display boards, numbered on both sides for clarity, shall be used to indicate the substitution of players and the number of minutes to be allowed for time lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equipment must be clear and visible for players, officials and spectators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Giant screens compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of giant screens must be in compliance with the relevant FIFA instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts must follow FIFA guidance on content, placement and operation of giant screens at stadiums.

rubrics_metrics.name: No smoking in competition/technical areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Smoking is not permitted in the technical area, in the vicinity of the field of play or within competition areas such as the dressing rooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smoking bans apply to all competition operational areas to protect player and spectator welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Football supply and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Footballs used in the preliminary competition shall be supplied by the host association. The visiting team shall be supplied with a sufficient quantity of the same ball for practice. Balls shall conform with the Laws of the Game and FIFA Equipment Regulations and bear one of: 'FIFA QUALITY PRO', 'FIFA QUALITY' or 'INTERNATIONAL MATCHBALL STANDARD (IMS)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts must supply officially certified balls and ensure visiting teams have matching practice balls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team equipment and prohibition of messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating associations shall comply with FIFA Equipment Regulations. Display of political, religious or personal messages or slogans by players and officials on playing or team kits, equipment or body is prohibited. Display of commercial messages/slogans by players/officials is not allowed during official FIFA activities (matches, training, press conferences, mixed-zone).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict neutrality required for team equipment during official events; FIFA issues specific equipment regulations to be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team kit colour declarations and goalkeeper kit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Each team shall inform FIFA of two differing and contrasting colours (one dark, one light) for official and reserve team kits and select three contrasting colours for goalkeepers that must be distinctly different from each other and from team kits. Teams must supply a set of goalkeeper shirts without names or numbers for emergency situations where an outfield player becomes goalkeeper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only declared colours may be worn; extra goalkeeper shirts ensure visible distinction if position changes during match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host and visiting teams’ kit choice in case of colour conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Each team shall in principle wear its official kit as declared. If colours may cause confusion the host team shall be entitled to wear its official kit and the visiting team shall use its reserve kit or a combination if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host has priority to wear official kit absent agreement; visiting team responsible to change to avoid clashes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Players’ sleeve badges and official graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA shall supply players’ sleeve badges with the official competition logo to be affixed on the right-hand sleeve and any other badge as stipulated to be affixed on the left-hand sleeve. FIFA will issue guidelines for use of official terminology and graphics and instructions for sleeve badges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations must follow FIFA-issued branding and placement instructions for sleeve badges and competition graphics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremonial elements (flags, anthems, music)
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA and the confederation concerned will determine exact ceremonial elements for each preliminary match and shall issue associations with guidelines for their implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts and associations must follow FIFA/confederation guidance on ceremonial protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and role of association media officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Each association shall appoint a dedicated media officer to facilitate cooperation between associations, FIFA and the media. The media officer shall be able to speak at least one official FIFA language (English, French, German or Spanish) and ensure media facilities and services meet required standards. The officer coordinates all media arrangements including pre/post-match press conferences and interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media officer is the primary liaison for accreditation, press activities and ensuring technical/media standards are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media accreditation and priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Associations’ media officers shall coordinate accreditation requests and ensure requests come from bona fide media representatives. Priority is given to media representatives from the countries of the two teams. FIFA, in cooperation with host, may establish accreditation terms and conditions for all matches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accreditation must be carefully vetted; FIFA retains rights to set accreditation policies and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-match media activities and minimum representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each association shall arrange a pre-match media activity on the day before each match (ideally a press conference; for lower-interest matches may be mixed-zone or single interview). As a minimum the activity shall be attended by the head coach and ideally a player. Host must provide necessary technical infrastructure including interpreting services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media activities are typically in the stadium unless an agreed alternative; media officers coordinate timing and logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training sessions open to media
rubrics_metrics.description: Both associations shall make their training sessions open to the media for at least 15 minutes on the day before the match. Official training sessions shall take place in the match stadium in principle. Media representatives shall be able to follow sessions from positions they will occupy during the match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access provisions specify minimum media access time and positioning consistent with matchday operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press seating and media working area requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An adequate number of covered seats shall be provided for the written press in a separate, secure area with clear view of the pitch and sufficient technical installations (power, internet). A working area with desks, power and cabled or Wi‑Fi internet connections shall also be provided; internet must be dedicated and provided free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts must ensure safe, functional and connected media workspaces to meet press reporting needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview restrictions and post-match arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are not permitted during the match on the field or immediate vicinity. Interviews with coaches and players are allowed upon arrival subject to agreement. Post-match 'flash' interviews shall be conducted in a designated area between the pitch and players’ dressing rooms. Associations must make their head coach and at least two key players available for interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict zones and times govern media interviews to preserve match integrity and player/team routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory mixed-zone and player obligation to pass through
rubrics_metrics.description: After the match a mixed zone shall be set up between dressing rooms and team transport area to offer media the opportunity to conduct interviews. All players listed on the official start list are obliged to pass through the mixed zone to conduct media interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mixed-zone obligations ensure media access to players post-match; teams must ensure player compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricted media access to dressing rooms with narrow exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Media representatives are forbidden from entering team and referee dressing rooms before, during and after the match. Exception: one of the host broadcaster’s cameras may enter the dressing rooms before the match at an agreed time to film players' shirts and equipment; this filming must be completed well before arrival of players.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dressing room privacy is protected; limited pre-approved broadcast filming is permissible under strict timing and control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field and tunnel media access limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: No media representatives are allowed to enter the field before, during or after the match except one hand-held camera crew covering team line-ups at the start and up to two host broadcaster cameras filming after the end of the match. Similar exceptions apply to tunnel and dressing-room area for flash interviews, arrivals and players in tunnel prior to pitch entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch and tunnel access is tightly restricted to accredited broadcast personnel with defined limited exceptions to minimize interference and safety risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited number of accredited production staff on pitch boundary
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a limited number of photographers, camera operators and production staff of broadcasters – equipped with appropriate pitch-access accreditation – shall be allowed to work in the area between the boundaries of the pitch and the spectators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host must control and limit pitchside media numbers to those accredited and necessary for broadcast/coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership and provision of match footage to FIFA
rubrics_metrics.description: All revenue from exploitation of commercial rights for preliminary competition matches belongs to the host association and, with ticket income, forms gross receipts. Owners of the rights are obliged to provide FIFA, upon request and free of charge, with 15 minutes of action footage per match. FIFA may use this footage free of charge for promotional purposes and its own electronic/multimedia carriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hosts retain commercial revenues but must supply FIFA with footage for FIFA promotional/multimedia use at no cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deduction of confederation levies from gross receipts
rubrics_metrics.description: The levies due to the confederation according to the confederation’s statutes and regulations shall be deducted from the gross receipts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial distributions follow confederation statutes; levies are deducted prior to other settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation on cost allocation between participating associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating member associations shall settle other costs among themselves. FIFA recommends that the visiting association pay for its delegation’s international travel to the venue or nearest international airport, as well as board, lodging and incidental expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associations should agree cost-sharing arrangements in line with these recommendations and local confederation practices.
